$comment: The coding agents MetaLoop can drive and the models it knows, read by crew.py and agent_run.py. Any other model id works in a pin too (give its window with @, e.g. codex/my-model:high@400k). Benchmark notes are dated; reference/crew.md has the sources. To refresh: edit this file and the presets in ../crews, and keep reference/crew.md in step.

claude.name: Claude Code
claude.sign_in: run `claude` once in a terminal and sign in, or set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
claude.guard: in-session hook (ctx_guard.py), with the wrapper as a backstop
claude.skills: the MetaLoop plugin (claude plugin install metaloop --marketplace jomitiron/MetaLoop)

codex.name: Codex CLI
codex.sign_in: run `codex` once and sign in with ChatGPT, or set CODEX_API_KEY
codex.guard: wrapper: estimated from the event stream; interrupt and resume to hand off
codex.permissions: --sandbox workspace-write (network on, the run folder writable) + git/gh guard rails

agy.name: Antigravity CLI
agy.install: Google's installer (antigravity.google/docs/cli); it puts agy in ~/.local/bin
agy.sign_in: run `agy` once and sign in with Google, or set GEMINI_API_KEY with modelProvider gemini in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json
agy.guard: wrapper: estimated from the event stream; interrupt and resume to hand off
agy.permissions: --dangerously-skip-permissions + git/gh guard rails (a refused tool is soft-denied and the run still exits 0)
agy.mcp: per run (.agents/mcp_config.json in the session's folder)

gemini.name: Gemini CLI
gemini.sign_in: GEMINI_API_KEY, or Vertex (GOOGLE_API_KEY with GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true). Since June 2026 Google serves personal plans through Antigravity (agy); Gemini CLI is for Code Assist Standard and Enterprise
gemini.guard: wrapper: estimated from the event stream; interrupt and resume to hand off
gemini.mcp: per run (.gemini/settings.json in the session's folder)

grok.name: Grok Build
grok.guard: wrapper: estimated from the event stream; interrupt and resume to hand off
grok.skills: .grok/skills or ~/.grok/skills (it also reads Claude Code plugins)

opencode.name: OpenCode
opencode.vendor: any provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, ...)
opencode.guard: wrapper: measured from each step's reported tokens; interrupt and resume to hand off
opencode.permissions: a per-run config (OPENCODE_CONFIG) allowing edits and commands + git/gh guard rails
opencode.mcp: per run (the same config's mcp section)

cursor.name: Cursor CLI
cursor.install: curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash (its binary is `agent`; METALOOP_BIN_CURSOR names another)
cursor.guard: wrapper: estimated from the event stream (Cursor reports no token usage); interrupt and resume to hand off
cursor.mcp: per run (.cursor/mcp.json in the session's folder, --approve-mcps)

models.label: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M)
models.notes: Terminal-Bench 4.1 65.8% (max, joint first) · SlopCodeBench 29.6% isolated solve at medium for $0.99 a checkpoint (best value of the top ten) · SWE-Atlas-QnA 65.9, the best single model in a stock CLI

models.label: Claude Fable 5.2 (1M)
models.notes: FrontierCode 2.0 49.2 (xhigh) / 48.7 (high), first: changes mergeable with no human edits · Terminal-Bench 4.1 65.8% (max, joint first, 3.5x Opus 5.5's cost) · start at high

models.label: Claude Haiku 5.5 (1M)
models.notes: Terminal-Bench 4.1 40.0%: too weak for chains; fine for a quick research question

models.label: GPT-6 Astra
models.notes: SlopCodeBench second at xhigh: 31.6% isolated, best strict solve (16.3%), least verbose code (0.158) · Terminal-Bench 4.1 60.3% (max) · LibraryDesignBench 44-45 · window unverified: set it with @

models.label: GPT-6.1 Sol
models.notes: SlopCodeBench 29.1% at medium for $0.91 a checkpoint · Terminal-Bench 4.1 60.9% (max) at about a seventh of Opus 5.5's run cost · the budget coder

models.label: Gemini 4 Carbon
models.notes: Terminal-Bench 4.1 64.6% (high) for about 30% of Opus 5.5's run cost · SWE-Atlas-QnA 63.7 · not on SlopCodeBench · `agy models` gives the exact slug

models.label: Grok 4.7
models.notes: Terminal-Bench 4.1 38.8% (Grok Build) · Artificial Analysis coding index 41.6: well behind the leaders on every coding benchmark found
